methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
AMP Robotics is a Series A-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $439.1M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the robotics sector, including same and adjacent-stage companies such as Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline ($30M), applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying a valuation of $60M. Peer-median analysis across the four most directly comparable robotics companies yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The stark divergence between methods reflects the substantial heterogeneity in the peer set, which spans seed through Series B stages.

The triangulated valuation range is $51M to $2.0B, with a median of $880M. This wide band reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation: the stage-progression method suggests a significantly lower valuation tied to capital deployed, while peer comps—dominated by Series B valuations—establish a substantially higher market precedent. Key uncertainties include whether AMP's capital efficiency and revenue generation warrant peer-level multiples and whether the diversity of peer stages materially affects comparability.
